title: Derived forgetting of fixed pairs and right derived functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ and $H:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D$ be additive autoequivalences, and use the fixed-pair categories $\mathcal C^F,\mathcal D^H$ [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Write $U_F,U_H$ for the forgetful functors. These fixed-pair categories are Grothendieck abelian. The functor $U_F$ is exact and conservative and has an exact left adjoint whose underlying object at $M$ is $\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}F^nM$, with the structure isomorphism shifting the summands (negative powers use a chosen quasi-inverse of $F$). It preserves injective objects and K-injective complexes, where K-injective means that every map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. The induced functor $D(U_F):D(\mathcal C^F)\to D(\mathcal C)$ on the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] is conservative.

Let $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be additive and left exact, with a natural isomorphism $e:H L\xrightarrow{\sim}L F$. Define $\widetilde L:\mathcal C^F\to\mathcal D^H$ by $\widetilde L(M,\theta)=(LM,L(\theta)\circ e_M)$. There is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$D(U_H)\,R\widetilde L\xrightarrow{\sim}RL\,D(U_F).$$
Here $R$ denotes total right derivation, computed by K-injective resolutions [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. This isomorphism identifies the derived-unit map $D(U_H)(\widetilde L(M)[0]\to R\widetilde L(M[0]))$ with the ordinary map $L(U_FM)[0]\to RL((U_FM)[0])$. Thus it identifies the actual derived comparison maps, as well as their objects.

proof.text: To prove derived conservativity, use the canonical cohomology comparison of the exact forgetful functor, as in [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. If the forgotten derived map is invertible, this comparison makes the forgotten cohomology map invertible in every integer degree. Conservativity of forget F then makes each cohomology map invertible. Apply DerivedCategory.isIso_iff, namely [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. This argument keeps the independently chosen derived-category universes.

proof.text: Fix the universally quantified witnesses hF and hC. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-exact-square-comparison] with Hprime = mapOfNatIso e, H = L, r = forget F and s = forget H. The square is definitionally commuting, r and s are exact, and r preserves K-injectives by the source instance of step 2. Use the universal properties of the chosen right-derived functors in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. This yields an isomorphism beta uniquely normalized on K-injective complexes: a_I followed by beta_QI equals b_I. Here a and b are the natural transformations formed from the two units and the canonical exact-localization factors, exactly as in the comparison theorem.

Extend the equality a followed by Qh(beta) = b to every homotopy object. Represent that object by a complex K and choose s:K to I using hF. Qh sends the homotopy class of s to an isomorphism, since quotientCompQhIso identifies it with Q(s). Naturality of the two transformations along s, their equality at I, and cancellation of the image of this isomorphism under B prove equality at K. This is the private proved helper homotopy_unit_ext. Finally multiply the component equation by the inverse square identification, the forgetful localization factor, and RL of the other localization factor. Cancellation gives exactly the displayed unit equation, with both mapHomotopyCategoryCompIso factors retained. Conversely the displayed equation gives a followed by Qh(gamma) = b by the inverse cancellation. Restrict this equation to K-injectives and invoke step 4 uniqueness to obtain gamma = beta.
